[{"sha":"a47a315dc4a9df129a2d8a1b030e73194c69d4b5","node_id":"C_kwDOFVKCydoAKGE0N2EzMTVkYzRhOWRmMTI5YTJkOGExYjAzMGU3MzE5NGM2OWQ0YjU","commit":{"author":{"name":"Jarred Sumner","email":"jarred@jarredsumner.com","date":"2026-10-31T19:15:32Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-31T19:15:32Z"},"message":"AOT: bun test --aot on large suites, module loading fixes, fuzzer fixes (#47316)

### What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #47129 for `bun build --compile --aot` and `bun test
--aot`.

Goes with oven-sh/WebKit#942, which is merged. `WEBKIT_VERSION` is
WebKit's `main` at `4d45755fed4a`, so oven-sh/WebKit#781 and
oven-sh/WebKit#945 reach Bun with this PR too, with and without `--aot`.

#### `bun test --aot`

- `spyOn()` and `mock.module()` work on compiled modules.
- They also reach the exports of a TypeScript package that has its own
`tsconfig.json`.
- Tests can spy on, assign, define, delete and restore members of
built-ins. Built-ins stay read-only in executables.
- `mock.module()` also works on JSON, text, TOML and YAML imports.
- `delete require.cache[path]` makes the next `require()` or `import()`
load the module again.
- A test file that fails to compile fails by itself instead of taking
the whole run down.
- A run is compiled as one program. A large suite under `--parallel` is
built in layers instead (more than 16 test files that reach more than 32
MB of source, on Linux, not hardened): the packages and Bun's library as
one image, the project's own files as a second, and the test files in
groups of 16 on top, built as workers need them. On one shard of a
private suite (3,052 test files, 16 cores) that takes 458 s at 24
workers, against 937 s for plain `bun test` at 8 workers, and the
largest builder needs 4.7 GB where one program needed 10.6 GB.
`BUN_DEBUG_TEST_AOT_WORDS=TestRunLayers:0`, `:1` or `:2` forces a form,
and such a run says its form in one line on stderr.
- In layers a worker that crashes costs the file it was running: the
file is reported as failed and the run goes on.
- `--timings=<file>` also reads a `memory` map, megabytes by test file.
No second file of over 1,024 MB starts while one runs.
`--update-timings` writes the map on Linux.
- The compiled program is handed to the test process through a memfd,
falling back to shm and then to an unlinked temp file.
- With `RegExp.prototype.exec` replaced, `text.replace(/b/, "-")` and
its like call the replacement.
- An internal compiler error names its source file, so the test files
that import it are dropped in one step.

#### Module loading

- `require(name)` and `await import(name)` with a computed name find
compiled CommonJS modules.
- An imported `.html` file that fails to bundle is a build error. A file
that's only passed to `require.resolve()` isn't bundled as a page (this
broke `playwright-core`).
- Fixed a build panic on some import cycles.
- A `throw` from a CommonJS module was lost in a CJS → ESM → CJS import
cycle.
- A file whose only CommonJS reference sits in dead code was treated as
CommonJS under `--aot` only.
- `require()` of a text file in a compiled executable matches `bun build
--compile`.
- Re-exporting one name from a `node:` module no longer compiles the
whole module.
- `--aot-log-type-mismatches` and `--compile-in-place` take emit options
from the working directory's `tsconfig.json`, as `bun run` does.
- `import(name)` and `require(name)` are narrowed by what the name can
be. On a large program with one such call, analysis went from 138 s to
19 s and peak memory from 11.2 GB to 5.1 GB.
- `ShadowRealm` in code that never runs no longer fails the build.

#### Other fixes

- Wrong results and compiler errors found by fuzzing and CI. Each has a
reproducer in `test/aot`.
- Use-after-free when spreading an object whose getter deletes
properties and triggers a GC.
- Crash in programs with more than 65,535 distinct property names.
- Segfault or a wrong sum in `bun test --aot` when a test puts a `Proxy`
under a prototype object.
- Segfault with two modules behind `import()`, each holding a `Proxy`
whose handler literal has the same shape, when only one of them is
loaded.
- `function* f(n) { yield "a"; if (!(n > 0)) return; f = g; yield* f(n -
1); }`: the second `[...f(1)]` didn't see `f = g`.
- In a very large function, `["run", ...(on ? ["--verbose"] : []),
name]` was one array shared by every call.
- Code nested more than 2,000 levels deep was refused.
- A caught `TypeError` cost more the larger the program and the longer
the function.
- `require("./d/" + name)`, where `bun build` doesn't link the call:
JavaScript under an unknown extension returned a path instead of
running, a `.sh` file returned `""`, and a file that isn't a program
returned a path where plain Bun throws.
- Five or more files embedded `with { type: "file" }` all failed to load
as Workers.
- A `FinalizationRegistry` stopped calling back once the closure that
names it died while a sibling closure of the same scope lived on.
- `x = null` on a local that's never read again didn't release the
object.
- `exports.p = v` was lost when a branch that never runs defines `p`
with `Object.defineProperty()`.
- Error positions inside constructors match plain Bun.
- `--trim`: a Worker started from code the build can't see gets the
interpreter, transpiler and loaders it needs.
- `"a" in proxy` and `for...in` gave wrong results when the key lives on
the prototype of a proxy's target.
- A `Symbol.species` getter on a user class could be left out of the
executable.
- `str.search()` with a frozen global or sticky regex didn't throw.
- React Compiler: a macro called inside a component ran twice.
- `--minify-identifiers`: a class with standard decorators keeps its
original name in `.name`, in the decorator's `context.name` and in stack
traces.
- `Object.getPrototypeOf()`, `Reflect.getPrototypeOf()` and `__proto__`
on `Bun.$`, `Bun.sql`, `console` and similar objects match plain Bun.
- React Compiler: template text that `minify.syntax` joined into one
string is no longer dropped.
- Compiled executables start on Android.
- A Bun built against a WebKit without AOT links again.

#### New

- `Bun.build({ compile })` accepts `aotValidate`, `aotCheck` and
`aotTesting`, matching the CLI flags. They're hidden, like `aotDisable`
and `aotHeat`. Builds that need JS plugins can now run under the
compiler's checker too.
- `--explain` points at where a value starts to escape, not at the last
hop.

#### Faster

- A compiled hello world starts with fewer instructions, page faults and
syscalls.
- Generators, one-shot property accesses and string building in loops
take fewer instructions.
- `localeCompare()` without a locale, `sort()` with a comparator, array
callbacks in untyped code and small `new Array(n)`.
- `f(...list)`, `list.push(...other)`, `instanceof` on functions below
functions, and a `switch` over the object that tsc, esbuild, swc or
babel emit for an enum.
- Whole-program analysis of a large test suite takes less than half the
memory and CPU it did.

#### Tests and CI

- Directives in `.ir` tests are parsed strictly. A misspelled directive
is an error instead of being treated as a comment.
- The test runner only unpacks the engine's shell and test binaries in
shards that use them, and uses `tar` on Windows.
- Removed the source-scanning checks, their two steps in `lint.yml` and
the `aot_check` build rule.

#### Not AOT-specific

These replace #47304.

- **Windows CI steps failed on some commit messages.**
`Launch-VsDevShell.ps1` reads the environment back line by line as
`NAME=VALUE`. `BUILDKITE_MESSAGE` holds the whole commit message, so any
line of it containing `=` was parsed as a variable, and some of those
names can't be set in PowerShell. `scripts/vs-shell.ps1` now unsets
multi-line variables around that call and restores them afterwards.
- **A build-scaling test was over its memory bound on macOS.** mimalloc
returns freed pages after a delay, and pages waiting to be returned
count toward peak RSS. `test/aot/build-scaling` now runs with
`MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0`. No bound was raised.
- `Bun.build()` with many chunks allocated memory proportional to the
square of the chunk count when computing chunk hashes.
- A Worker's `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` went silent for good
after an out-of-memory error during a write.
- FreeBSD decompresses ICU's data at startup, matching the WebKit build
(about 13 MB smaller, Android too).
- uSockets checks its allocations.
- An error at a shorthand property (`{ name }`) is reported at the name.

#### Changes that also touch plain Bun

- `bun test --files-from <list>`, `--timings=<json>` and
`--update-timings`.
- The Rust allocator's `realloc()` moves a block of up to 64 KB when it
shrinks into a smaller size class. `mi_realloc()` leaves a block where
it is while it stays half full, so `shrink_to_fit()` and
`into_boxed_slice()` gave nothing back.
- Under `bun test --isolate`, three things kept every finished test
file's realm alive: the functions that `bun:sql` hands to native code,
streams that were never cancelled, and the cached Structure of a
`RegExp`'s `groups` object (that one is in oven-sh/WebKit#942).
- The crash handler answers a `SIGBUS` among files that the compiler has
mapped for reading with "a source file was made shorter while it was
being compiled".
- `posix_spawn` keeps the highest `ru_maxrss` of the children it has
reaped, for the `memory` map.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Every fix has a test in `test/aot` that fails without it.
- Differential fuzzing against plain Bun on Linux x64 and arm64.
- The stored programs also run under ASAN and the GC verifier.
